sights.address: Coney Island, Punggol, Singapore (West entrance off Punggol Promenade / East entrance off Pasir Ris side; to confirm at geocode)
sights.w: A 133-hectare island off Punggol, once owned by the Aw brothers of Tiger Balm. In 1950 it was sold to a businessman who planned a resort modelled on New York's Coney Island. Since October 2015 a 50-hectare NParks park has kept it deliberately rustic: casuarina woods, a 2.5 km car-free trail, hidden beaches and bridges at both ends to the mainland.

sights.address: Punggol Point foreshore (Punggol Point Park), Punggol, Singapore
sights.w: A National Heritage Board historic site. On 23 February 1942, during the Japanese Sook Ching operation, a Hojo Kempei firing squad killed some 300–400 Chinese civilians on the Punggol foreshore. Human remains turned up in the sand in 1977 and 1997. An NHB marker set up in 1995, for the 50th anniversary of the end of WWII, records the killings.

A seafront park at the northern tip of Punggol, opened on 20 November 2011 at the old Punggol Point fishing-village beach. People come for the sunset over the Strait of Johor, the jetty views across to Malaysia, and the WWII Sook Ching memorial on its foreshore.

sights.address: Waterway Point, beside Punggol MRT/Punggol Waterway, Punggol, Singapore (street + postal to confirm at geocode)
sights.w: Punggol's main mall, with more than 200 stores, on the banks of Punggol Waterway next to the MRT. It is the town's main food cluster, covered in its own Eatbook food guide, and the jumping-off point for the waterway park.
